title: rpw-rushpro-2003-heavyweight
label: Gideon Poe

won.source: The fed's write-ups of the Adrenaline shows of 18 and 25 January 2004, which replay the finish of the Genesis main event of 11 January 2004; the card of Genesis itself is not held.

note: Gideon Poe hit El Diablo with the Cadaver Theory and pinned him to become the first RPW World Heavyweight Champion at Genesis, a show whose write-up has not been loaded. Defences on record. Adrenaline 10, 25 January 2004: Gideon Poe hit Peter Maxwell with the Cadaver Theory, then flew off the turnbuckle with the Suicide Anthem and pinned him, with Jason O'Neil counting as special guest referee, to retain the World Heavyweight Championship. Adrenaline 18, 28 March 2004: Gideon Poe kicked Nascosto Nerezza in the throat and covered him without hooking the leg to retain the World Heavyweight Championship. Adrenaline 20, 11 April 2004: Gideon Poe dropped to his knees with Christian Alexander Kannon over his shoulder for a backdrop piledriver and pinned him to retain the World Heavyweight Championship in a triple threat with Jason O'Neil.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-heavyweight
label: Invincible Gabe

lost.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 24 and Adrenaline 25: the first has Invincible Gabe as champion going into The Kannon Effect, the second has Karina Wolfenden as the new champion from it; the pay-per-view's own card is not held.

note: SOURCES DISAGREE — Argyle's booking record dates Adrenaline 23 as 25 April 2004; the show's own page dates it 9 May 2004 from the fed's own news posts, and this history follows the page. Invincible Gabe won the World Heavyweight Championship in a six way when Christian Alexander Kannon restarted the match as sudden death, because Gideon Poe had tapped out to Magnum Wolf's Triangle Hold while Gabe's pin on Violence Jack was being counted, and Gabe hit Wolf with the Apocalyptic Chartbusting Last Dancing Stone Gabe Stunner and pinned him. A defence is on record. Adrenaline 23, 9 May 2004: Invincible Gabe retained the World Heavyweight Championship by count out after Gideon Poe left the ring to save Quinton Dufresne from Peter Maxwell's chair and was still on the ramp at the count of ten.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-heavyweight
label: Karina Wolfenden

won.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 24 and Adrenaline 25: the first has Invincible Gabe as champion going into The Kannon Effect, the second has Karina Wolfenden as the new champion from it; the pay-per-view's own card is not held.

note: SOURCES DISAGREE — The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 32 has Karina Wolfenden say she overcame five of the roster's best and that Gideon Poe handed her the belt; the write-up of Adrenaline 25 has her take it from Gabe at The Kannon Effect after he lay down. The date window rests on the first account, and both are recorded. Argyle's booking record dates Adrenaline 30 as 4 July 2004; the show's own page dates it 11 July 2004 from the fed's own news posts, and this history follows the page. Argyle's booking record dates Adrenaline 32 as 18 July 2004; the show's own page dates it 25 July 2004 from the fed's own news posts, and this history follows the page. Karina Wolfenden took the World Heavyweight Championship from Invincible Gabe at The Kannon Effect, a pay-per-view whose card is not held; the write-up of the next show has Gabe say he lay down for her. Defences on record. Adrenaline 30, 11 July 2004: Magnum Wolf swatted Tessa Windsor off the top rope with a steel chair and the bell rang, so the match ended with no decision and Karina Wolfenden kept the World Heavyweight Championship. Adrenaline 32, 25 July 2004: Karina Wolfenden hit Brian Arson with a Pump Dropkick and caught him in a Small Package for the three after Christian Alexander Kannon had a replay show Magnum Wolf knocking her foot off the rope and the match continued, so she retained the World Heavyweight Championship.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-eclipse
label: Karina Wolfenden

lost.source: The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 4, which has Ilan Levin defending the title he won the week before from Karina Wolfenden; the show of 23 November 2003 is not held.

note: Karina Wolfenden retrieved the belt from above the ring in a six-person ladder match to become the first Eclipse Champion, ahead of Lumi, Ilan Levin, A.J. Trinidad, The Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid and El Diablo. A defence is on record. Adrenaline 2, 16 November 2003: Karina Wolfenden hooked The Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid's legs after pulling him in over the top rope with a Huricanrana from the apron and pinned him to retain the Eclipse Title.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-eclipse
label: Ilan Levin

won.source: The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 4, which has Ilan Levin defending the title he won the week before from Karina Wolfenden; the show of 23 November 2003 is not held.

note: Ilan Levin pinned Karina Wolfenden to win the Eclipse Title while El Diablo was on the outside, on Adrenaline 3, a show whose write-up has not been loaded; the record is the recap in Adrenaline 4. A defence is on record. Adrenaline 4, 30 November 2003: El Diablo hit Ilan Levin with the Brain Disorder as the time limit expired before the referee finished the three count, so the match was ruled a time limit draw and Levin kept the Eclipse Title.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-eclipse
label: Karina Wolfenden

lost.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 10, which has Karina Wolfenden as champion, and Adrenaline 17, where Carys enters as the Eclipse champion with the belt; the change is on no card that is held.

note: Karina Wolfenden hit Ilan Levin with the Three Sixty Alien Drop and pinned him in a three way with Brianna Washington to win the Eclipse Title back. Defences on record. Adrenaline 9, 18 January 2004: Karina Wolfenden hit The Hardcore Isosceles Trapezoid with the Whirlwind Romance, a tornado seatbelt DDT, onto a chair and pinned him to retain the Eclipse Title in the first match under the new Eclipse Rules. Adrenaline 10, 25 January 2004: Karina Wolfenden sprang off the ropes with a Huricanrana that drove Violence Jack's head onto a chair and pinned him with his legs locked to retain the Eclipse Title, after Magnum Wolf had hit Jack with a chair while she was tied in the ropes.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-eclipse
label: Carys

won.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 10, which has Karina Wolfenden as champion, and Adrenaline 17, where Carys enters as the Eclipse champion with the belt; the change is on no card that is held.

note: Carys became the Eclipse Champion after Karina Wolfenden; the change of hands is on no card that is held. Defences on record. Adrenaline 20, 11 April 2004: Carys hit Quinton Dufresne in the face with a shovel and pinned him to retain the Eclipse Title. Adrenaline 21, 18 April 2004: Carys covered Tessa Windsor and got the three after Chris Storm hit Tessa in the back with the Mid South belt as she came off the ropes, so Carys retained the Eclipse Title in a no disqualification match.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-eclipse
label: Gideon Poe
note: Gideon Poe spiked Carys with the Unholy Confession, a cradle tombstone piledriver, and pinned her in a five way to win the Eclipse Title.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-tag-team
label: Invincible Gabe and Rampage

won.source: The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 17, which announces them as the new champions after the show of the Sunday before; that show's card is not held.

lost.source: The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 25, which says the champions lost the titles at The Kannon Effect; the pay-per-view's own card is not held.

note: Invincible Gabe and Rampage won the Tag Team Titles at an Adrenaline show before 21 March 2004 that is not held; the write-up names Sweet Illusion among the teams they beat. Defences on record. Adrenaline 18, 28 March 2004: Scott "Rampage" Matthews lifted James Edwards in the Electric Chair and Invincible Gabe hooked the leg for the three, so Invincibleness~! retained the Tag Team Titles in their first defence against Christian Crawford and Edwards. Adrenaline 20, 11 April 2004: Invincible Gabe and Rampage retained the Tag Team Titles by count out when the three men of The Phantom Swerve~! ran to the back and Mike Matslap counted to ten.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-tag-team
label: The Forsaken

won.source: The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 25, which says the champions lost the titles at The Kannon Effect; the pay-per-view's own card is not held.

note: The Forsaken took the Tag Team Titles from Invincible Gabe and Rampage at The Kannon Effect, a pay-per-view whose card is not held; Rampage was pinned, and the write-up of the next show bills Gabe and Rampage as the former tag champions.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-mid-south
label: Chris Storm

won.source: The fed's write-up of Adrenaline 17, which names Chris Storm as the Mid South Champion; the day he won the belt is not on record.

lost.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 24, which has Chris Storm as champion, and Adrenaline 25, which has Tessa Windsor as the newly crowned champion after The Kannon Effect; the pay-per-view's own card is not held.

note: SOURCES DISAGREE — The write-up of Adrenaline 17 calls Chris Storm "STILL RPW Mid South champion" but never says the belt was on the line, and has him bring neither belt to the ring; Argyle's own title line records it as a defence. Both readings are recorded. Chris Storm was the Mid South Champion by 21 March 2004; the write-ups say he won a tournament for the belt, which is on no card that is held. Defences on record. Adrenaline 17, 21 March 2004: Chris Storm hit Malphas with the Perfect Storm and pinned him on the referee's five count to retain the Mid South Title. Adrenaline 20, 11 April 2004: Chris Storm hit Karina Wolfenden with the RyoPlex and pinned her to retain the Mid South Title. Adrenaline 21, 18 April 2004: Chris Storm hit Kohana with the Cherry Blossom, a Hangman's DDT from the second rope, and pinned him to retain the Mid South Title.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-mid-south
label: Tessa Windsor

won.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 24, which has Chris Storm as champion, and Adrenaline 25, which has Tessa Windsor as the newly crowned champion after The Kannon Effect; the pay-per-view's own card is not held.

lost.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 25, which has Tessa Windsor as champion, and of Adrenaline 30 and 31, which say Shawn Stewart won the title from her the week before the first of them; the match is on no card that is held.

note: Tessa Windsor beat Chris Storm cleanly at The Kannon Effect, a pay-per-view whose card is not held, to become the Mid South Champion. A defence is on record. Adrenaline 25, 30 May 2004: Referee Chris Faircount called for the bell when Steven Silver would not let go of a choke on Tessa Windsor, so the Mid South Title match ended in a disqualification and Windsor kept the title.

title: rpw-rushpro-2003-mid-south
label: Shawn Stewart

won.source: The fed's write-ups of Adrenaline 25, which has Tessa Windsor as champion, and of Adrenaline 30 and 31, which say Shawn Stewart won the title from her the week before the first of them; the match is on no card that is held.

note: SOURCES DISAGREE — Argyle's booking record dates Adrenaline 31 as 11 July 2004; the show's own page dates it 18 July 2004 from the fed's own news posts, and this history follows the page. Shawn Stewart took the Mid South Title from Tessa Windsor in the week before the Adrenaline of 11 July 2004; the match is on no card that is held. A defence is on record. Adrenaline 31, 18 July 2004: Shawn Stewart locked El Spiffy! in the Mordida da Pantera, a guillotine choke, and Spiffy tapped out, so Stewart retained the Mid South Title.
